web_evidence.title: Mad Honey: A GMA Book Club Pick
web_evidence.note: The publisher's authorized Chapter 1 excerpt is headed Olivia and sustains first-person narration; it also supplies the missing context that resolves q06929 as Olivia's narration.

web_evidence.title: Jodi Picoult Writing Styles in Mad Honey
web_evidence.note: The structural study guide explicitly identifies the novel as first-person and says its chapters alternate between Olivia's and Lily's perspectives.

web_evidence.title: Jennifer Finney Boylan's new novel with Jodi Picoult is literally a dream come true
web_evidence.note: The reported author interview confirms that Olivia and Lily are the book's two character voices, that their chapters alternate, and that the Lily sequence moves backward while Olivia's moves forward.

web_evidence.title: Book Review: Mad Honey
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly describes two first-person narratives, with Olivia and Lily narrating alternating chapters in opposite chronological directions.

web_evidence.title: Bucknell Forum | Jodi Picoult | Season 5 | Episode 2
web_evidence.note: In this author interview, Picoult identifies Olivia and Lily as the novel's narrators and explains that the coauthors each switched to the other's narrator for one chapter, corroborating the two-narrator structure.

search_log: Searched for the verified title and authors with excerpt, first chapter, point of view, first person, narrator, and alternating-narrator terms.
Opened the Penguin Random House Library Marketing edition page and inspected its authorized Olivia Chapter 1 excerpt.
Searched for and opened author interviews about the division between Olivia's and Lily's chapters, including Central Maine, Costco Connection, an Independent podcast transcript, and PBS.
Opened a whole-book point-of-view study and a detailed review explicitly identifying both narratives as first person.
Checked the author-hosted Mad Honey book-club-kit result, but the PDF redirect could not be opened safely, so it was not used as evidence.
Opened a Penguin UK PDF returned by the search, determined that its Evelyn-and-Lily passage belonged to a different work despite the misleading result, and excluded it.
person_note: The book uses two sustained participating narrators, Olivia and Lily, and both narrate in first person. Their chapters alternate and their timelines run in opposite directions, but multiple first-person narrators remain FIRST rather than ALTERNATING under the methodology. Numerous event quotations independently expose I, me, my, or story-specific we narration from these voices; speech, recipes, bee lore, and universal-you aphorisms were treated as non-base. The publisher excerpt confirms Olivia's first-person opening and resolves the otherwise clipped q06929, while whole-book structural sources explicitly confirm that Lily's alternating chapters are also first person. No credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person base sections was found.
